Title: A Great Nation and Blessing Through Abraham
Promise: Through Abraham God would make a great nation, bless him, and bless all families of the earth in him.
Fulfillment: Galatians 3:8 states the gospel was preached beforehand to Abraham in this promise, and Galatians 3:16 identifies the Seed as Christ.

Title: The Land Promised to Abraham's Seed
Promise: God would give the land of Canaan to Abraham and his seed.
Fulfillment: Joshua 21:43-45 states the LORD gave Israel all the land he swore to give their fathers and that none of his good promises failed.

Title: A Saviour From the Seed of the Woman
Promise: The seed of the woman would bruise the serpent's head, the first promise of a deliverer after the fall.
Fulfillment: Matthew 1:22-23 states the virgin birth of Jesus fulfilled what was spoken by the prophet.

Title: God's Presence With Jacob
Promise: God would be with Jacob, keep him wherever he went, and bring him back to the land.

Title: Deliverance From Egypt
Promise: God would bring Israel out of affliction in Egypt into a land flowing with milk and honey.
Fulfillment: Exodus 14:30 states the LORD saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians.

Title: A Treasured Possession and Holy Nation
Promise: If Israel obeyed God's voice and kept his covenant, they would be his peculiar treasure above all people, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.
Condition: If ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant.

Title: Rest in the Land
Promise: God would give Israel rest from all their enemies and a place to dwell securely.
Fulfillment: Joshua 21:44 states the LORD gave them rest round about according to all he swore to their fathers.

Title: An Everlasting House for David
Promise: God would raise up David's seed after him, establish his kingdom, and build him a house; his throne would be established for ever.
Fulfillment: Luke 1:32-33 states the Lord God would give Jesus the throne of his father David and that his kingdom would have no end.

Title: The New Covenant
Promise: God would make a new covenant, writing his law in hearts, forgiving iniquity and remembering sin no more.
Fulfillment: Hebrews 8:8-12 quotes this passage as the new covenant, and Luke 22:20 records Jesus instituting it in his blood.
FulfillmentScriptures: Hebrews 8:8; Hebrews 8:9; Hebrews 8:10; Hebrews 8:11; Hebrews 8:12; Luke 22:20

Title: Return From Exile After Seventy Years
Promise: After seventy years in Babylon, God would visit his people and bring them back to Jerusalem.
Fulfillment: Ezra 1:1-3 records Cyrus' decree for the return and the rebuilding of the house of the LORD at Jerusalem.

Title: The Outpouring of the Spirit
Promise: God would pour out his Spirit upon all flesh, and sons and daughters would prophesy.
Fulfillment: Acts 2:16-17 records Peter declaring at Pentecost, 'this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel'.

Title: The Gift of the Holy Spirit
Promise: To those who repent and are baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, God gives the gift of the Holy Ghost, a promise to them, their children, and all afar off.
Condition: Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins.

Title: Forgiveness on Confession
Promise: If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Condition: If we confess our sins.

Title: Healing and Restoration on Repentance
Promise: If God's people humble themselves, pray, seek his face, and turn from wicked ways, he will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
Condition: If my people humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways.

Title: Eternal Life to Believers
Promise: Whoever believes in the Son has everlasting life; God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son.
Condition: Belief in the Son.

Title: Never Left nor Forsaken
Promise: God will never leave nor forsake his people; he goes with them and will not fail them.

Title: Peace in Trouble
Promise: Christ gives his peace, not as the world gives, and the peace of God guards hearts and minds.
Condition: In Philippians: prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, instead of anxiety.

Title: Rest for the Weary
Promise: All who labour and are heavy laden are invited to come to Christ, who will give them rest.
Condition: Come unto me; take my yoke upon you, and learn of me.

Title: Strength for the Weak
Promise: God gives power to the faint and increases strength to those with no might; those who wait upon the LORD renew their strength.
Condition: Waiting upon the LORD.

Title: Provision for Needs
Promise: Those who seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness will have all necessary things added to them; God supplies all need according to his riches in Christ.
Condition: Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.

Title: Wisdom to Those Who Ask
Promise: If any lack wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives liberally and does not reproach, and it shall be given him.
Condition: Ask in faith, nothing wavering (James 1:6).

Title: The Holy Spirit to Those Who Ask
Promise: A heavenly Father gives the Holy Spirit to them that ask him, as earthly fathers give good gifts to their children.
Condition: Ask, seek, knock.

Title: Prayer According to His Will
Promise: If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us; whatever we ask in Christ's name, he will do.
Condition: Asking according to his will, in Christ's name.
KeyScriptures: Matthew 7:7; Matthew 7:8; John 14:13; John 14:14; 1 John 5:14; 1 John 5:15

Title: Comfort in Trouble
Promise: God comforts his people in all their tribulation, and the God of all comfort strengthens them to comfort others.

Title: Resurrection of the Dead
Promise: Christ is the resurrection and the life; believers will rise, the dead in Christ rising first at his coming.
KeyScriptures: John 11:25; John 11:26; 1 Corinthians 15:20; 1 Corinthians 15:21; 1 Corinthians 15:22; 1 Corinthians 15:23; 1 Thessalonians 4:16

Title: No Condemnation in Christ
Promise: There is no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus; whoever hears his word and believes has passed from death unto life.
Condition: Being in Christ Jesus; hearing and believing.

Title: Victory Over Sin and Death
Promise: Sin shall not have dominion over believers, and thanks be to God who gives the victory through Jesus Christ.

Title: Kept From Falling
Promise: God is able to keep believers from falling and to present them faultless before his glory with exceeding joy; no one can pluck them out of Christ's hand.

Title: God's Word Accomplishes Its Purpose
Promise: God's word goes forth and does not return void; it accomplishes what he pleases and prospers in the thing whereto he sent it.

Title: Refuge and Protection
Promise: He that dwells in the secret place of the most High abides under the shadow of the Almighty; God delivers and honours those who love him.
Condition: Dwelling in the secret place; loving God and knowing his name.

Title: Guidance for the Path
Promise: God's word is a lamp to feet and a light to the path; acknowledging him in all ways, he directs paths.
Condition: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; in all thy ways acknowledge him.

Title: A New Heaven and a New Earth
Promise: God will make all things new: a new heaven and a new earth, no more death, sorrow, crying, or pain, God dwelling with men.

Title: Christ's Return
Promise: Jesus will come again and receive his people to himself, descending from heaven with a shout, the voice of the archangel, and the trump of God.

Title: Healing to the Prayer of Faith
Promise: The prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; God is the LORD that healeth.
Condition: The prayer of faith; confession and prayer for one another (James 5:16). No promise is made about timing or manner of healing.

Title: Protection for Cain
Promise: God assured Cain that anyone who killed him would face sevenfold vengeance, and he set a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would strike him down.

Title: Covenant With Noah in the Ark
Promise: God pledged to establish his covenant with Noah, so that Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives would enter the ark and be preserved through the flood.
Fulfillment: Genesis 7:7 records Noah entering the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.

Title: Seasons Continue and the Ground No Longer Cursed
Promise: After the flood, God pledged never again to curse the ground on account of humanity, nor to strike down every living thing as he had done, and he assured that the yearly cycle of sowing and reaping, temperature extremes, seasons, and the alternation of day and night would persist as long as the earth lasted.

Title: Never Again a Flood to Destroy All Flesh
Promise: God established his covenant with Noah, his seed, and every living creature, pledging that never again would all flesh be cut off by flood waters, nor would a flood again destroy the earth, and he set the bow in the cloud as the sign that he would remember that covenant.

Title: Offspring as Numerous as the Stars
Promise: God told Abraham to count the stars if he could, and assured him that his offspring would be just as countless.

Title: Judgment on the Oppressor and Departure With Great Substance
Promise: God assured Abraham that the nation which afflicted his seed would be judged, and that afterwards his seed would come out with great substance.
Fulfillment: Exodus 12:36 records that Israel asked for and received articles of silver, gold, and raiment from the Egyptians, so that they spoiled Egypt.

Title: Ishmael Multiplied and Made a Great Nation
Promise: God assured Abraham and Hagar that Ishmael's seed would be multiplied exceedingly, that twelve princes would come from him, and that he would be made a great nation, because he was Abraham's seed.
Fulfillment: Genesis 25:16 records twelve princes descended from Ishmael, named by their towns and castles.

Title: An Everlasting Covenant and Kings From Abraham
Promise: God established an everlasting covenant with Abraham and his seed after him, to be their God, and he assured Abraham that nations and kings would come from him, and that Canaan would be an everlasting possession for his seed.

Title: A Son for Sarah and Covenant With Isaac
Promise: God assured Abraham that Sarah would bear him a son at the set time in the following year, that the child would be called Isaac, and that God would establish his covenant with Isaac and his seed after him.
Fulfillment: Genesis 21:2 records that Sarah bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken.

Title: Seed Multiplied and Blessing Confirmed by Oath
Promise: After Abraham obeyed in offering Isaac, God swore by himself that he would greatly bless Abraham, multiply his seed as the stars of heaven and the sand on the seashore, give his seed possession of the gate of their enemies, and bless all nations of the earth in his seed.
Condition: Abraham's obedience in the offering of Isaac, as stated in the passage itself.

Title: God With Jacob in Egypt and His Return
Promise: God told Jacob not to fear going down into Egypt, assuring him that a great nation would be made of him there, that God would go down with him into Egypt, that God would also surely bring him up again, and that Joseph would be with him at his death.

Title: God's Presence With Moses
Promise: God assured Moses that he would certainly be with him, and that the token would be that after bringing the people out of Egypt they would serve God on the mountain.

Title: Speech Given to Moses and Aaron
Promise: God assured Moses that he would be with his mouth and teach him what to say, and that he would likewise be with Aaron's mouth, teaching them both what to do, with Aaron speaking to the people in Moses' place.

Title: A Redeemed People and the Promised Land
Promise: God pledged to bring Israel out from under Egyptian burdens, free them from bondage, redeem them with a stretched-out arm and great judgments, take them as his own people and be their God, and bring them into the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and give it to them as a heritage.
Fulfillment: Exodus 14:30 records the LORD saving Israel that day from the Egyptians, and Joshua 21:43 records the LORD giving Israel all the land he swore to give their fathers.

Title: Passover Protection for Marked Houses
Promise: God assured Israel that the blood on the doorposts would be a token, and that when he saw the blood he would pass over the house, so that the plague would not destroy them when he struck Egypt.
Condition: Blood of the lamb applied to the doorposts, as the passage itself requires.

Title: Diseases Withheld at Marah
Promise: At Marah, God pledged that if Israel diligently listened to his voice, did what was right in his sight, gave ear to his commandments, and kept all his statutes, he would put none of the diseases of Egypt upon them, for he is the LORD who heals them.
Condition: Diligently listening to God's voice, doing right in his sight, giving ear to his commandments, and keeping all his statutes.

Title: Long Life for Honouring Parents
Promise: God pledged that honouring father and mother would lead to a long life in the land he was giving to Israel.
Condition: Honouring father and mother.

Title: An Angel to Guard the Way and Give the Land
Promise: God pledged to send an angel before Israel to keep them on the journey and bring them to the prepared place, to oppose their enemies and fight their adversaries, to cut off the peoples of the land, to put dread before them, to clear out the inhabitants gradually rather than in a single year, and to fix their territory stretching between the southern sea and the Philistine coast, and between the wilderness and the great river, handing the inhabitants over to them.
Condition: Obeying the angel's voice and doing all that God spoke.
KeyScriptures: Exodus 23:20; Exodus 23:22; Exodus 23:23; Exodus 23:27; Exodus 23:30; Exodus 23:31

Title: Blessing, Health, and Full Days in the Land
Promise: God pledged that if Israel served the LORD, he would bless their bread and water, take sickness away from among them, allow none to cast their young or be barren in the land, and fulfil the number of their days.
Condition: Serving the LORD their God.

Title: God Dwelling Among Israel
Promise: God pledged to make his home in the midst of Israel and to stand as their God, so that they would recognize him as the LORD who rescued them from Egypt precisely in order to live among them.
Fulfillment: Exodus 40:34 records the glory of the LORD filling the tabernacle after it was set up.

Title: God's Presence and Rest
Promise: After the golden calf, God assured Moses that his presence would go with them and that he would give them rest.

Title: Provision in the Sixth Year
Promise: God pledged to command his blessing on Israel in the sixth year, so that the land would bring forth fruit for three years, covering the sabbath year and the year after until the new harvest came in.
Condition: Keeping the sabbath year for the land, as the passage itself frames it.

Title: Blessings for Obedience
Promise: God pledged that if Israel walked in his statutes and kept his commandments, he would give rain in due season, fruitful land and trees, bread to the full, peace in the land with none making them afraid, safety from evil beasts and the sword, and his tabernacle among them, walking among them and being their God while they were his people.
Condition: Walking in God's statutes and keeping and doing his commandments.

Title: Covenant Remembered After Confession
Promise: God pledged that if Israel confessed their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, he would remember his covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, and remember the land, and would not cast them away or abhor them to destroy them utterly or break his covenant, because he is the LORD their God.
Condition: Confession of their own iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, with humbled hearts accepting punishment.

Title: The LORD Will Bless His People
Promise: God commanded the Aaronic blessing to be spoken over the children of Israel, that the LORD would bless them and keep them, make his face shine upon them and be gracious to them, lift up his countenance upon them and give them peace, and he pledged that in putting his name upon them he would bless them.

Title: Remembrance and Deliverance in Battle
Promise: God pledged that when Israel went to war against an enemy oppressing them and blew an alarm with the trumpets, they would be remembered before the LORD their God and saved from their enemies.
Condition: Going to war against an oppressing enemy and blowing an alarm with the trumpets.

Title: Spirit Upon the Seventy Elders
Promise: God pledged to share the empowering spirit resting on Moses with seventy Israelite elders, so that they would help carry the people's load and Moses would not carry it by himself.
Fulfillment: Numbers 11:25 records the LORD coming down, taking of the spirit upon Moses, and giving it to the seventy elders, who prophesied.

Title: Caleb and Joshua Brought Into the Land
Promise: God pledged that Caleb, who had another spirit and wholly followed him, would be brought into the land he had searched, with his seed possessing it, and that Caleb and Joshua alone of their generation would come into the land sworn to their fathers.
Condition: Caleb wholly following the LORD, as the passage itself states.
Fulfillment: Joshua 14:13 records Joshua blessing Caleb and giving him Hebron for an inheritance, and Joshua 14:14 records that Hebron became Caleb's inheritance because he wholly followed the LORD.

Title: The Children Brought Into the Land
Promise: God pledged that the little ones of Israel, whom their parents said would be a prey, would be brought into the land which their parents had despised, and that they would know that land.

Title: The LORD the Levites' Inheritance
Promise: God told Aaron that he would have no inheritance in the land among Israel, because the LORD himself would be his part and his inheritance, and he gave the Levites the tithes of Israel as an inheritance in return for the service of the tabernacle.

Title: Life to Those Who Look at the Serpent
Promise: God pledged that a serpent of brass set upon a pole would bring life to everyone bitten by the fiery serpents who looked upon it.
Condition: Looking upon the serpent of brass after being bitten.
Fulfillment: Numbers 21:9 records Moses making a serpent of brass and setting it on a pole, and that everyone bitten who looked upon it lived.

Title: A Covenant of Peace and Everlasting Priesthood for Phinehas
Promise: God granted Phinehas a peace covenant, with priesthood continuing permanently through his descendants, in recognition of his ardent stand for God and his act that turned aside wrath from Israel.
Condition: Phinehas's zeal for God and atonement for Israel, as the passage itself states.

Title: Mercy on Return in Tribulation
Promise: God assured Israel that if in tribulation they sought him and returned to the LORD, they would find him when they sought him with all their heart and soul, and that the LORD, being merciful, would not forsake them, destroy them, or forget the covenant sworn to their fathers.
Condition: Seeking the LORD with all heart and soul and returning to him in tribulation.

Title: Covenant Mercy to a Thousand Generations
Promise: God assured Israel that he remains faithful across a thousand generations toward people who love him and obey his commands, honouring his covenant bond with them and showing them steadfast mercy.
Condition: Loving God and keeping his commandments.

Title: Blessing to Lend to Many Nations
Promise: God pledged that if Israel carefully listened to his voice and kept his commandments, the LORD would greatly bless them in the land, they would lend to many nations and not borrow, and they would reign over many nations while none reigned over them.
Condition: Carefully listening to God's voice and keeping all his commandments.

Title: A Prophet Like Moses
Promise: God pledged to raise up a prophet from among Israel's brethren, like Moses, and to put his words in that prophet's mouth, so that the prophet would speak all that God commanded, with God requiring it of anyone who would not listen to his words.
Fulfillment: Acts 3:22 records Peter quoting Moses' words about a prophet like him, and Acts 3:23 records that every soul who would not hear that prophet would be destroyed from among the people.

Title: The LORD Fights for Israel in Battle
Promise: God assured Israel that when they went out to battle against a greater host, they should not be afraid of horses, chariots, or a greater people, because the LORD their God was with them, and he himself would go with them to fight for them against their enemies and save them.

Title: Return, Gathering, and a Circumcised Heart
Promise: God pledged that when Israel returned to the LORD and obeyed his voice with all their heart and soul, he would turn their captivity, have compassion on them, gather them from all the nations where he had scattered them, bring them into the land their fathers possessed so they would possess it and be multiplied above their fathers, and circumcise their hearts and the hearts of their seed so that they would love the LORD with all their heart and soul and live.
Condition: Returning to the LORD and obeying his voice with all heart and soul.

Title: Joshua to Bring Israel Into the Land
Promise: God charged Joshua to take courage, assuring him that he would lead Israel into the territory pledged to their ancestors, with God standing alongside him.
Fulfillment: Joshua 3:17 records all Israel passing clean over Jordan on dry ground under Joshua's leadership.

Title: God's Presence With Joshua
Promise: God would be with Joshua as he had been with Moses, and no opponent would stand against him all his life.
Fulfillment: The conquest narrative records victory after victory under Joshua, and Joshua 11:23 states Joshua took the whole land.

Title: Jericho Given to Joshua
Promise: God had already given Jericho, its king, and its mighty men of valour into Joshua's hand.
Fulfillment: Joshua 6:20 records that when the people shouted, the wall fell down flat and they took the city.

Title: Ai Given to Joshua
Promise: God had already given the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land into Joshua's hand.
Fulfillment: Joshua 8:21 records that Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city.

Title: Victory Over the Five Kings
Promise: God had already delivered the allied kings and their forces into Joshua's hand, and none of them would stand before him.
Fulfillment: Joshua 10:10 records that the LORD discomfited the enemy before Israel and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon.

Title: Victory Over the Northern Kings
Promise: By the next day at about that time, God would deliver all the northern kings slain before Israel.
Fulfillment: Joshua 11:8 records that the LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel, who smote them and chased them.

Title: The Remaining Nations Driven Out
Promise: God himself would drive out the remaining hill-country peoples and Sidonians from before Israel, while Israel divided the land by lot as its inheritance.
Fulfillment: The conquest drove out many peoples, though Judges 1 records that Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants of the land.

Title: Judah to Go Up First
Promise: Judah would go up first, for God had already delivered the land into Judah's hand.
Fulfillment: Judges 1:4 records that the LORD delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand.

Title: Sisera Delivered to Barak
Promise: God would draw Sisera, with his chariots and multitude, to the river Kishon and deliver him into Barak's hand.
Fulfillment: Judges 4:15 records that the LORD discomfited Sisera and all his chariots and host before Barak.

Title: Midian Defeated by Gideon
Promise: God would surely be with Gideon, and Gideon would defeat the Midianites completely, as though facing a single man.
Fulfillment: Judges 7:22 records that the Midianite host fled when the three hundred blew their trumpets.

Title: Deliverance by the Three Hundred
Promise: By the three hundred men who lapped, God would save Israel and deliver the Midianites into Gideon's hand.
Fulfillment: Judges 7:22 records that the Midianite host fled when the three hundred blew their trumpets.

Title: Samson to Begin Israel's Deliverance
Promise: The promised son would be a Nazarite from the womb, and he would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines.
Fulfillment: Judges 13:24 records the birth of Samson, who went on to strike the Philistines.

Title: Benjamin Delivered to Israel
Promise: If Israel went up again against Benjamin, God would deliver the Benjamites into their hand the next day.
Fulfillment: Judges 20:35 records that the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel that day.

Title: A Faithful Priest Raised Up
Promise: God would raise up a faithful priest who would act according to God's heart and mind, give him an enduring household, and keep him ministering before God's anointed always.
Fulfillment: Solomon removed Abiathar from the priesthood and put Zadok in his place, as 1 Kings 2:35 records.

Title: Deliverance Through Saul
Promise: The man from Benjamin whom Samuel was to anoint would save God's people from the Philistines.
Fulfillment: 1 Samuel 14:23 states the LORD saved Israel that day in the battle that followed Saul's leadership at Michmash.

Title: Keilah Delivered to David
Promise: God would deliver the Philistines at Keilah into David's hand.
Fulfillment: 1 Samuel 23:5 records that David fought the Philistines, smote them with a great slaughter, and saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

Title: Recovery From the Amalekites
Promise: If David pursued the Amalekite troop, he would surely overtake them and recover everything without fail.
Fulfillment: 1 Samuel 30:18-19 records that David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away, with nothing lacking.

Title: Victory at Baal-perazim
Promise: God would certainly deliver the Philistines into David's hand.
Fulfillment: 2 Samuel 5:20 records that David smote them at Baal-perazim, where the LORD broke forth upon his enemies.

Title: Victory at the Mulberry Trees
Promise: When David heard marching sounds above in the mulberry grove, the LORD would advance ahead of him to strike the Philistine army.
Fulfillment: 2 Samuel 5:25 records that David did so and smote the Philistines from Geba to Gazer.

Title: Wisdom, Riches, and Honour for Solomon
Promise: God had given Solomon a wise and understanding heart, unmatched before or after, and had also given him riches and honour beyond any king of his days.
Condition: Lengthened days depended on walking in God's ways and keeping his statutes and commandments, as David did.
Fulfillment: 1 Kings 4:29 states God gave Solomon wisdom, and 1 Kings 10:23 states he exceeded all kings in riches and wisdom; the lengthened days depended on obedience, and Solomon later turned aside, as 1 Kings 11:4 records.

Title: God Dwelling Among Israel in the Temple
Promise: If Solomon walked in God's statutes, executed his judgments, and kept all his commandments, God would carry out what he had promised David, make his dwelling with the Israelites, and never abandon them.
Condition: Walking in God's statutes, executing his judgments, and keeping all his commandments.
Fulfillment: At the dedication, the cloud filled the house and the glory of the LORD filled the house, as 1 Kings 8:11 records.

Title: The Temple Hallowed and the Throne Established
Promise: God had heard Solomon's prayer and hallowed the temple he built, so that God's name would be there for ever, with his eyes and heart there perpetually; and if Solomon walked as David had, God would establish his kingdom's throne over Israel for ever.
Condition: Walking before God as David did, in integrity of heart and uprightness, keeping his statutes and judgments.
Fulfillment: The temple stood as God's house, but the everlasting throne depended on walking as David did, and 1 Kings 11:11 records the kingdom rent from Solomon's son for his disobedience.

Title: One Tribe Preserved for David's Sake
Promise: For David's sake and Jerusalem's sake, God would not tear the whole kingdom away, but would leave one tribe to Solomon's son.
Fulfillment: 1 Kings 12:20 records that none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only.

Title: Ten Tribes Given to Jeroboam
Promise: God would tear the kingdom from Solomon's hand and give ten tribes to Jeroboam, leaving one tribe to Solomon's son so that David would always have a light before God in Jerusalem.
Condition: The sure house depended on hearkening to all God commanded, walking in his ways, and keeping his statutes and commandments, as David did.
Fulfillment: 1 Kings 12:20 records that all Israel made Jeroboam king, with only Judah following the house of David; the sure house depended on obedience he did not keep.

Title: Meal and Oil That Will Not Fail
Promise: The barrel of meal would not run out and the cruse of oil would not fail until the day God sent rain on the earth.
Fulfillment: 1 Kings 17:16 records that the barrel of meal wasted not and the cruse of oil did not fail, according to the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah.

Title: Rain Sent Upon the Earth
Promise: God would send rain upon the earth, and told Elijah to show himself to Ahab.
Fulfillment: 1 Kings 18:45 records that the heaven grew black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain.

Title: Deliverance From Syria at Samaria
Promise: God would deliver the great Syrian multitude into Ahab's hand that very day, so that Ahab would know the LORD is God.
Fulfillment: 1 Kings 20:21 records that the king of Israel went out and slew the Syrians with a great slaughter.

Title: Deliverance From Syria at Aphek
Promise: Because the Syrians claimed the LORD was only God of the hills, God would deliver their great army into the king of Israel's hand.
Fulfillment: 1 Kings 20:29 records that in the seventh day the battle was joined and the children of Israel slew one hundred thousand Syrian footmen in one day.

Title: The Moabites Delivered to Israel
Promise: As well as providing water, God would deliver the Moabites into the hands of the allied kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 3:24 records that when the Moabites came to the camp, the Israelites rose up and smote them so that they fled.

Title: A Son for the Shunammite
Promise: About that season, in the course of a year, the Shunammite woman would embrace a son.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 4:17 records that the woman conceived and bore a son at that season, as Elisha had said.

Title: Plenty in Samaria by Tomorrow
Promise: By the next day at about that time, fine flour and barley would be selling cheaply in the gate of Samaria.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 7:18 records that it came to pass as the man of God had spoken, with flour and barley at those prices in the gate of Samaria.

Title: Jehu's Sons to the Fourth Generation
Promise: Because Jehu had done what was right in executing judgment on the house of Ahab, his line would hold Israel's throne for four generations.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 15:12 states this was the word of the LORD spoken to Jehu, and adds that so it came to pass.

Title: The Sign of Victory Over Syria
Promise: Joash would strike the Syrians in Aphek until he had consumed them, as a sign of the LORD's rescue from Syria.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 13:25 records that Joash beat Ben-hadad three times and recovered the cities of Israel.

Title: Jerusalem Defended From Assyria
Promise: The king of Assyria would not enter Jerusalem, shoot an arrow there, or cast a bank against it, but would return by the way he came, for God would defend the city to save it, for his own sake and for David's sake.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 19:35 records that the angel of the LORD went out and smote one hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians that night.

Title: Hezekiah Healed and Given Fifteen Years
Promise: God had heard Hezekiah's prayer and seen his tears, and would heal him so that he would go up to the house of the LORD on the third day, add fifteen years to his life, and deliver him and Jerusalem from the king of Assyria, defending the city for God's own sake and for David's sake.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 20:7 records that the boil was treated and Hezekiah recovered.

Title: Josiah Gathered in Peace
Promise: Josiah would be gathered to his fathers and to his grave in peace, and his eyes would not see all the evil God would bring upon Jerusalem.
Fulfillment: Josiah was slain at Megiddo, as 2 Kings 23:29 records, yet before Jerusalem's destruction, so he did not live to see the evil foretold for the place.

Title: Solomon, a Man of Rest and Temple Builder
Promise: A son would be born to David who would be a man of rest, with rest from all his enemies, named Solomon, bringing peace and quietness to Israel in his days; he would build a house for God's name, be God's son, and have his kingdom's throne established over Israel for ever.
Fulfillment: Solomon sat on the throne of David and his kingdom was established greatly, as 1 Kings 2:12 records, and he built the house and finished it, as 1 Kings 6:14 records.

Title: God Found by Those Who Seek Him
Promise: God would stay with Asa and Judah while they stayed with him, and would be found by them when they sought him.
Condition: Being with the LORD and seeking him.
Fulfillment: Asa sought the LORD, and 2 Chronicles 15:15 states the LORD gave them rest round about.

Title: Victory Without Fighting
Promise: Judah would not need to fight this battle, but only to take their stand, stand still, and watch the LORD's salvation with them, for the battle belonged to God.
Fulfillment: 2 Chronicles 20:22 records that the LORD set ambushments against Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, and 2 Chronicles 20:24 records that Judah found only dead bodies, with none escaped.

Title: God Arises to Set the Needy in Safety
Promise: When the poor are oppressed and the needy sigh, God himself rises up and places the needy person in safety away from those who scorn him.

Title: Taken Up When Forsaken
Promise: Even if a person's own father and mother abandon them, the LORD will receive them and take care of them.
Condition: Being forsaken by father and mother.

Title: The Righteous Are Preserved and Inherit the Land
Promise: The meek will inherit the earth and delight in abundant peace; the righteous will inherit the land and live in it for ever, preserved by the LORD, who helps, delivers, and saves them from the wicked because they trust in him.
Condition: Meekness, waiting on the LORD, and trust in him.

Title: Deliverance, Preservation, and Strength for Those Who Care for the Poor
Promise: The LORD will rescue in trouble, preserve alive, and bless the person who considers the poor, and will strengthen that person on a bed of sickness rather than handing them over to their enemies.
Condition: Considering the poor.

Title: Sustained and Never Moved
Promise: Those who hand their burdens over to the LORD will be upheld by him and kept steady, never left to collapse.
Condition: Casting one's burden on the LORD.

Title: No Good Thing Withheld from the Upright
Promise: The LORD, who is a sun and a shield, will give grace and glory to his people and will not keep back any good thing from those who walk uprightly.
Condition: Walking uprightly.

Title: God Accepts Job's Prayer for His Friends
Promise: God told Eliphaz and his two friends to offer a burnt offering and have Job pray for them, committing himself to accept Job's prayer on their behalf rather than dealing with them for their folly.
Condition: Offering the burnt offering as commanded, with Job praying for them.
Fulfillment: Job 42:9 records that the friends did as the LORD commanded them and that the LORD accepted Job.

Title: The Sign of Immanuel
Promise: God would give the house of David a sign: a young woman would bear a son, and his name would declare that God is with his people.
Fulfillment: Matthew's Gospel applies this sign to the birth of Jesus.

Title: A Child Is Born, a Son Is Given
Promise: A child would be born to rule, carrying the government on his shoulder, and his reign on David's throne would grow without end in justice and righteousness.
Fulfillment: Luke's Gospel presents Jesus as the heir who will sit on David's throne.

Title: The Branch From Jesse
Promise: A shoot would grow from Jesse's line, filled with the Spirit and with wisdom, judging justly for the poor, and his reign would bring a peace in which former enemies dwell together and the earth is full of knowledge of the LORD.
Fulfillment: Paul quotes the root of Jesse as the one in whom the Gentiles trust.

Title: Death Swallowed Up in Victory
Promise: God would put an end to death itself and wipe tears from every face, removing his people's reproach from the whole earth.
Fulfillment: Paul quotes the swallowing up of death in victory in his teaching on resurrection.

Title: Perfect Peace for the Trusting Mind
Promise: God would keep in complete peace the person whose mind rests steadily on him, because that person trusts in him.
Condition: Trusting in the LORD with a mind stayed on him.

Title: The Ransomed Return to Zion
Promise: Those God ransoms would come back to Zion with singing and lasting joy, and sorrow and sighing would flee away.
Fulfillment: The return from Babylon under Cyrus is recorded in Ezra, though the everlasting joy described here points beyond that return.

Title: Help for the Fearful
Promise: God would be with his people, strengthen them, and hold them up, taking them by the hand and helping them, so they need not fear or be dismayed.

Title: Through the Waters and the Fire
Promise: God, who formed and redeemed his people, would be with them when they pass through deep waters and through fire, so the waters would not overwhelm them and the flame would not consume them.

Title: Spirit Poured on Offspring
Promise: God would pour water on thirsty ground and his Spirit on his people's descendants, so that they would grow like plants beside flowing streams.

Title: A Light to the Gentiles
Promise: God's servant would be more than Israel's restorer: he would be a light to the nations, so that God's salvation would reach to the ends of the earth.
Fulfillment: Simeon calls Jesus a light to the Gentiles, and Paul and Barnabas quote this passage for their mission to the Gentiles.

Title: An Unshakable Covenant of Peace
Promise: Even if mountains moved and hills were shaken, God's kindness would not depart from his people and his covenant of peace would not be taken away.

Title: An Everlasting Covenant of David's Sure Mercies
Promise: God would make an everlasting covenant with his people, giving them the sure, faithful mercies once promised to David.
Fulfillment: Paul quotes the sure mercies of David in connection with the resurrection of Jesus.

Title: Revival for the Contrite
Promise: God, who dwells on high, would also dwell with the humble and contrite in spirit, reviving the spirit of the humble and the heart of the contrite.
Condition: A contrite and humble spirit.

Title: The Redeemer and His Covenant
Promise: A Redeemer would come to Zion for those who turn from transgression, and God's covenant with them would stand: his Spirit upon them and his words in their mouths would not depart from them or their descendants.
Condition: Turning from transgression.
Fulfillment: Paul quotes the Deliverer coming to Zion and the covenant of taking away sins.

Title: The Anointed One Brings Liberty
Promise: God's anointed one would bring good news to the meek, bind up the brokenhearted, proclaim liberty to captives and the opening of prison doors, and comfort all who mourn.
Fulfillment: Jesus reads this passage in the synagogue at Nazareth and applies it to himself.

Title: The Righteous Branch
Promise: God would raise up for David a righteous Branch who would reign as king, deal wisely, execute justice and righteousness in the land, and in his days Judah would be saved and Israel dwell safely, under the name that declares the LORD is our righteousness.
Fulfillment: Luke's Gospel presents Jesus as the heir who will sit on David's throne.

Title: A Heart to Know the LORD
Promise: God would set his eyes on the exiles for good, bring them back to the land, build them up rather than pull them down, and give them a heart to know him, so that they would be his people and he would be their God, as they return to him wholeheartedly.
Condition: Returning to the LORD with the whole heart.
Fulfillment: The return to the land is recorded in Ezra.

Title: Israel Shall Never Cease as a Nation
Promise: As surely as the fixed order of sun, moon, and stars stands before God, Israel would never cease from being a nation before him, and his people would not be cast off for all they have done.

Title: Gathered With One Heart and an Everlasting Covenant
Promise: God would gather his people from all the lands where he had driven them, bring them back to their place, give them one heart and one way so they would fear him always, make an everlasting covenant with them to do them good and never turn away, and plant them in the land in faithfulness.
Fulfillment: The gathering is recorded in the return from exile, and the everlasting covenant is instituted by Jesus at the Last Supper.

Title: An Answer When You Call
Promise: God promised Jeremiah that if he called to him, he would answer and show him great and hidden things he did not know.
Condition: Calling upon the LORD.

Title: An Everlasting Covenant Remembered
Promise: Though Jerusalem had broken her covenant from her youth, God would remember his covenant with her from those days and establish an everlasting covenant with her, and she would know that he is the LORD when he forgives her past.

Title: The LORD Himself Will Shepherd His Flock
Promise: God himself would search for his scattered sheep, seek them out as a shepherd seeks a scattered flock, gather them from the peoples, feed them on good pasture, seek the lost, bring back the driven away, bind up the broken, and strengthen the sick.
KeyScriptures: Ezekiel 34:11; Ezekiel 34:12; Ezekiel 34:13; Ezekiel 34:14; Ezekiel 34:15; Ezekiel 34:16

Title: A New Heart and a New Spirit
Promise: God would sprinkle clean water on his people, take away their stony heart and give them a heart of flesh, put his Spirit within them so they would walk in his statutes, and they would dwell in the land given to their fathers as his people, with him as their God.

Title: The Waste Places Rebuilt
Promise: God would cleanse his people, cause the ruined cities to be inhabited, and make the desolate land like a garden, so that onlookers would know that he is the LORD who builds the ruins and plants what was desolate.
Fulfillment: Rebuilding after the exile is recorded in Nehemiah.

Title: Dry Bones Made Alive
Promise: God would open the graves of his people, bring them up out of their graves into the land of Israel, put his Spirit in them so they would live, and place them in their own land, so they would know that he is the LORD who has spoken and performed it.

Title: David the Shepherd and the Covenant of Peace
Promise: God would set one shepherd over his people, David his servant, who would feed them and be their prince, and God would make an everlasting covenant of peace with them, set his sanctuary among them forever, and be their God while they are his people.
Fulfillment: Luke's Gospel presents Jesus as the heir who will sit on David's throne.

Title: A Kingdom That Shall Never Be Destroyed
Promise: In the days of earthly kingdoms, the God of heaven would set up a kingdom that would never be destroyed nor left to another people, that would break in pieces all other kingdoms and stand forever.
Fulfillment: Revelation presents the kingdom of the world becoming the kingdom of the Lord and of his Christ.

Title: The Son of Man's Everlasting Dominion
Promise: One like a Son of man would come with the clouds of heaven, be brought before the Ancient of Days, and receive dominion, glory, and a kingdom, so that all peoples, nations, and languages would serve him, in a dominion that is everlasting and shall not pass away.
Fulfillment: Jesus speaks of the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

Title: Resurrection to Everlasting Life
Promise: Many who sleep in the dust of the earth would awake, some to everlasting life, and the wise would shine brightly, while those who turn many to righteousness would shine enduringly like stars.
Fulfillment: Jesus teaches of an hour when all in the graves will hear his voice and come forth.

Title: Sons of the Living God
Promise: Though Israel's number had been compared to the sand of the sea, in the very place where it was said they were not God's people, they would be called sons of the living God, and the children of Judah and Israel would be gathered together under one head.
Fulfillment: Paul quotes the calling of those who were not God's people as sons of the living God.

Title: Betrothed Forever
Promise: God would betroth his people to himself forever, in righteousness and judgment, in lovingkindness and mercies, and in faithfulness, so that they would know the LORD.

Title: They Shall Seek the LORD and David Their King
Promise: After many days, the children of Israel would return and seek the LORD their God and David their king, and would fear the LORD and his goodness in the latter days.
Fulfillment: Luke's Gospel presents Jesus as the heir who will sit on David's throne.

Title: Healing for the Backsliding
Promise: God would cure his people's turning away and love them without holding back, turning his anger away from them.
Condition: Returning to the LORD, as Hosea 14:1 calls Israel to do.

Title: Restoration of the Locust Years
Promise: God would restore to his people the years the locusts had eaten, and they would eat in plenty and be satisfied, praising the name of the LORD their God, and never be ashamed.
Condition: Returning to the LORD with all the heart, as Joel 2:12-13 calls Israel to do.

Title: Deliverance for All Who Call on the LORD
Promise: Whoever calls on the name of the LORD would be delivered, for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there would be deliverance, among the remnant whom the LORD calls.
Condition: Calling on the name of the LORD.
Fulfillment: Peter quotes this promise on the day of Pentecost, and Paul quotes it for all who call on the Lord.

Title: Life for Those Who Seek the LORD
Promise: God told Israel to seek him, and they would live, rather than seeking places of empty worship.
Condition: Seeking the LORD.

Title: The Fallen Tabernacle of David Raised Up
Promise: God would raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, close its breaches, raise up its ruins, and build it as in days of old, so that the remnant and the nations called by his name would be possessed.
Fulfillment: James quotes this passage at the Jerusalem council for the inclusion of the Gentiles.

Title: Planted, Never to Be Plucked Up
Promise: God would bring back his people's captivity, and they would build waste cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and gardens and eat their fruit, and be planted on their land, never again to be pulled up out of it.
Fulfillment: The return and rebuilding are recorded in Ezra and Nehemiah; the never-plucked permanence remains future in the passage's own terms.

Title: Deliverance on Mount Zion
Promise: On Mount Zion there would be deliverance and holiness, the house of Jacob would possess its possessions, deliverers would rise on Mount Zion to govern Esau's mountain, and the LORD's kingdom would stand.

Title: Nations to Zion in Lasting Peace
Promise: In the last days the mountain of the LORD's house would be established above the hills, all nations would flow to it to learn his ways and walk in his paths, the law would go forth from Zion, and nations would turn their weapons of war into farming tools and learn war no more, each sitting under his own vine and fig tree with none to make them afraid.

Title: The Lame Gathered and the LORD Reigning in Zion
Promise: God would assemble the halt and the outcast and those he had afflicted, make the lame a remnant and the outcast a strong nation, and the LORD would reign over them in Mount Zion from that time onward and forever.

Title: The Ruler From Bethlehem
Promise: From Bethlehem Ephratah, small among Judah's thousands, would come forth a ruler for Israel whose goings forth are from of old, from everlasting, and he would stand and feed his flock in the strength of the LORD.
Fulfillment: Matthew's Gospel quotes this passage for the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem.

Title: Pardon, Mercy, and Covenant Faithfulness
Promise: God, who pardons iniquity and delights in mercy, would not retain his anger forever, would have compassion on his people, subdue their iniquities, put their sins away from them entirely, and perform the truth to Jacob and the mercy to Abraham sworn to the fathers.

Title: A Pure Language for All Peoples
Promise: God would turn to the peoples a pure language, so that they might all call on the name of the LORD and serve him with one consent.

Title: The LORD Rejoicing Over Zion
Promise: Zion would sing and shout, for the LORD had taken away her judgments and cast out her enemy, and the King of Israel, the LORD himself, would be in her midst, so she would not see evil any more; he would save her, rejoice over her with joy, rest in his love, and joy over her with singing.

Title: The Outcasts Gathered and Given Praise
Promise: God would undo those who afflict his people, save her that halts, gather her that was driven out, give them praise and fame in every land where they had been put to shame, and bring them back and turn their captivity before their eyes.
Fulfillment: The return from exile is recorded in Ezra; the praise and fame described here go beyond that return.

Title: Glory of the Latter House and Peace
Promise: God would shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land, and all nations, and the desire of all nations would come, and he would fill the house with glory, with the glory of the latter house greater than that of the former, and in that place he would give peace.
Fulfillment: Hebrews quotes the shaking of heaven and earth from this passage.

Title: Zerubbabel, the LORD's Signet
Promise: God would take Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, as his servant, make him as a signet ring, and declare that he had chosen him.

Title: God Dwelling in the Midst of Zion
Promise: God told the daughter of Zion to sing and rejoice, for he would come and dwell in her midst, and many nations would be joined to the LORD in that day and become his people, and he would dwell in her midst, so she would know that the LORD of hosts had sent him.

Title: The Branch and Iniquity Removed in One Day
Promise: God would bring forth his servant the Branch, set a stone engraved before Joshua, and remove the iniquity of the land in a single day.

Title: The Branch Shall Build the Temple
Promise: The man whose name is the Branch would grow up out of his place, build the temple of the LORD, bear the glory, sit and rule on his throne as a priest on his throne, with the counsel of peace between them both.

Title: Gathered From East and West
Promise: God would save his people from the east country and the west country, bring them to dwell in Jerusalem, and they would be his people while he would be their God in truth and righteousness.
Fulfillment: The gathering is recorded in the return from exile in Ezra.

Title: The Humble King Riding on an Ass
Promise: Zion's king would come to her just and having salvation, lowly and riding on an ass, and he would cut off the chariot and the horse and the battle bow, speak peace to the heathen, and his dominion would stretch from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth.
Fulfillment: Matthew's Gospel quotes the king coming on an ass for Jesus' entry into Jerusalem, and John does the same.

Title: The Spirit of Grace and the Pierced One
Promise: God would give the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit marked by grace and prayer, and they would look with grief on the one they had pierced, mourning as for a firstborn son.
Fulfillment: John's Gospel quotes the looking on him whom they pierced at the crucifixion.

Title: A Spring of Cleansing Opened
Promise: In that day a spring of cleansing would be opened for the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.

Title: The LORD King Over All the Earth
Promise: The LORD would be king over all the earth, and in that day there would be one LORD and his name one.
Fulfillment: Revelation presents the kingdom of the world becoming the kingdom of the Lord and of his Christ.

Title: The Messenger Preparing the Way
Promise: God would send his messenger to prepare the way before him, and the Lord whom his people seek would suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant in whom they delight.
Fulfillment: Matthew's Gospel and Mark's Gospel quote the messenger preparing the way for John the Baptist.

Title: Blessing Without Limit
Promise: God invited his people to test him in giving: if they brought all the tithes into the storehouse, he would pour out blessing from heaven without limit, and would rebuke the devourer for their sake.
Condition: Bringing all the tithes into the storehouse.

Title: Righteousness Dawning With Healing
Promise: To those who fear God's name, righteousness would dawn like the sun, bringing healing, and they would go forth freely and flourish like young animals released to pasture.
Condition: Fearing the name of the LORD.

Title: Elijah Before the Great Day
Promise: Before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD, God would send Elijah the prophet, who would turn the heart of the fathers to the children and the heart of the children to their fathers, so the land would not be smitten with a curse.
Fulfillment: Jesus teaches that Elijah has already come, and the disciples understand him to mean John the Baptist.

Title: Two Nations in Rebekah's Womb
Promise: God revealed to Rebekah that her twins would found two distinct peoples, that the two groups would diverge from birth, that one would prove stronger than the other, and that the older child's line would end up serving the younger's. Doubt: This reads as a prophetic oracle about the future of two nations, not a divine commitment of benefit to Rebekah herself; no 'I will' promise is addressed to her, and the elder-serving-younger outcome is national history rather than a promised blessing.

Title: The LORD Shall Fight for You
Promise: Moses urged Israel to stay calm and watch for deliverance, telling them God would take up their battle for them and they need not fight for themselves. Doubt: The words are Moses speaking to the people, not a direct divine 'I will' speech in the text, and the assurance is tied to one battle at the Red Sea rather than a standing covenant promise; it also overlaps the deliverance promise already covered at Exodus 3:7-8.

Title: A Great Nation From Moses After the Golden Calf
Promise: God told Moses to step aside so that divine anger could wipe out Israel, offering instead to build a great nation through Moses alone. Doubt: This is a contingent proposal in anger that Moses intercedes against and God then does not carry out in that form; it is not a settled promise, since the narrative immediately turns on Moses' plea and God's relenting.

Title: Marvels Before the People
Promise: In renewing the covenant, God pledged to perform unprecedented wonders in front of the whole people, so that everyone would recognize the scale of what God was doing among them. Doubt: This is a general covenant-renewal summary of God's wonderful works rather than a specific promised benefit, and its substance overlaps the deliverance and conquest promises already drafted; it is unclear whether it should stand alone.

Title: Mercy and Forgiveness Proclaimed at Sinai
Promise: God described his own character as compassionate, patient, rich in loyal love and faithfulness, forgiving wrongdoing across generations, yet never treating the guilty as though they were innocent. Doubt: This is a proclamation of God's character and attributes, not a future commitment phrased as a promise to a recipient; treating an attribute statement as a promise would stretch the definition, though it underlies many promises.

Title: Life in the Statutes
Promise: God directed Israel to live by his rules and judgments, with the assurance that the person who kept them would find life through them. Doubt: This is a general principle linking obedience with life rather than a specific divine commitment to a person or people on an occasion; it is also a wisdom-like maxim, which the definition excludes, and its exact sense of 'live' is debated.
Condition: Doing God's statutes and judgments.

Title: Flesh for a Whole Month
Promise: God instructed Moses to tell the complaining people they would receive meat every day for a full month, until the supply itself became repulsive to them. Doubt: The provision is explicitly punitive, given in anger at the people's weeping and contempt, and ends in loathing and plague; it is doubtful whether a judgment-provision of this kind belongs in a collection of God's promises.

Title: God Going Before Israel Across the Jordan
Promise: Moses told Israel that God himself would cross ahead of them and clear away the nations on the other side, with Joshua crossing ahead of the people as their leader. Doubt: The words are Moses speaking about God rather than a direct divine speech in the text, and the substance duplicates the drafted conquest promises in Exodus 23 and Deuteronomy 20; it may be a restatement rather than a distinct promise.

Title: Prosperity Through the Book of the Law
Promise: If Joshua meditated on the book of the law day and night and observed all that was written in it, his way would prosper and he would have good success. Doubt: Part of the same Joshua 1 commissioning speech as the clear presence entry; listing it separately would split one speech, but its condition (meditation on the law) differs from the unconditional presence promise.
Condition: Meditating on the book of the law day and night and observing all that is written in it.

Title: The Nations Driven Out Before Israel
Promise: The living God was among Israel and would without fail drive out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites from before them. Doubt: Spoken by Joshua to the people, not in divine first person, and its substance restates the land and conquest promises already covered.

Title: Honour for Those Who Honour God
Promise: Those who honour God would be honoured by him, while those who despise him would be lightly esteemed. Doubt: A general principle embedded in a judgment speech against Eli's house; the promissory half is inseparable from the judgment half, which reverses the earlier promise to Eli's house.
Condition: Honouring God.

Title: Blessing for Fearing and Serving the LORD
Promise: If Israel feared the LORD, served him, obeyed his voice, and did not rebel, then both they and their king would continue following the LORD their God. Doubt: General covenant conditional blessing in Samuel's farewell address rather than a distinct divine commitment to a named recipient or occasion; verse 15 is the warning half of the same conditional.
Condition: Fearing the LORD, serving him, obeying his voice, and not rebelling against his commandment.

Title: A King Provided Among Jesse's Sons
Promise: God had provided himself a king among the sons of Jesse. Doubt: Announcement of a provision already being enacted (David's anointing follows immediately in the same chapter) rather than a future commitment made to a recipient.
Fulfillment: David, a son of Jesse, was anointed in the same chapter.

Title: A Child Named Josiah Born to David's House
Promise: A future descendant of David's line, named Josiah, would sacrifice the high-place priests upon the Bethel altar and burn human bones on it. Doubt: Predictive prophecy naming a future king, fulfilled centuries later, but framed as foretelling rather than a commitment made to a recipient; its main clause is judgment on the altar.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 23:16 records Josiah taking bones from the sepulchres and burning them upon the altar at Bethel.

Title: Food Enough and Left Over
Promise: The hundred men would eat and leave food over, according to the word of the LORD. Doubt: Genuine 'thus saith the LORD' wording, but a single-meal provision announcement, minor in scope beside the sustained provision entry from 1 Kings 17:14.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 4:44 records that they ate and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD.

Title: Cleansing by Washing in the Jordan
Promise: If Naaman washed seven times in the Jordan, his flesh would come again like a little child's and he would be clean. Doubt: Healing instruction with a promised outcome, spoken by Elisha without 'thus saith the LORD' framing; closer to a prophetic prescription than a divine promise speech.
Condition: Washing seven times in the Jordan.
Fulfillment: 2 Kings 5:14 records that Naaman dipped himself seven times and his flesh came again like a little child's, and he was clean.

Title: Israel's Coast Restored by Jonah's Word
Promise: Israel's territory would be restored from the Hamath frontier to the lowland sea, as the LORD had spoken through Jonah. Doubt: Promise content is reported, not quoted: the text says Jeroboam restored the coast 'according to the word of the LORD... by Jonah' without quoting the word itself, so the promise wording cannot be verified from this book.
Fulfillment: The restoration itself is recorded in the same verse.

Title: The LORD Able to Give Much More
Promise: The LORD was able to give Amaziah much more than the hundred talents he had paid for Israel's army. Doubt: States God's ability, not a commitment that he will give; assurance rather than promise, and no giving is recorded in the passage.

Title: Joy After Weeping
Promise: Sorrow lasts only for a night, and joy arrives with the morning, because God's favour gives life. Doubt: Reads as a general rhythm of sorrow turning to joy rather than an explicit divine commitment; no promise verb or divine speaker.

Title: God Will Instruct and Guide
Promise: God himself will instruct and teach the person he addresses, showing them the way to go and guiding them with his eye. Doubt: Genuine first-person divine promise, but its substance overlaps the existing 'Guidance for the Path' entry (Psalms 119:105; Proverbs 3:5-6).

Title: Deliverance Out of All Troubles
Promise: When the righteous cry out, the LORD hears them and rescues them from every trouble, however many their afflictions. Doubt: Overlaps the existing 'Refuge and Protection' entry (Psalms 91) and 'Comfort in Trouble' (Psalms 23:4).

Title: Preservation Going Out and Coming In
Promise: The LORD will keep his people from all evil, guarding their souls and watching over their going out and coming in for ever. Doubt: Overlaps the existing 'Refuge and Protection' entry (Psalms 91); preservation substance is the same.

Title: Unmovable as Mount Zion
Promise: Those who trust in the LORD stand firm like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, with the LORD surrounding his people for ever. Doubt: A simile of security rather than a stated commitment; overlaps protection and kept-from-falling themes already covered.
Condition: Trust in the LORD.

Title: Deliverance from Death and Keeping Alive in Famine
Promise: The LORD watches over those who fear him and hope in his mercy, rescuing them from death and keeping them alive in famine. Doubt: Overlaps the existing 'Refuge and Protection' entry; deliverance/preservation substance is the same.
Condition: Fearing the LORD and hoping in his mercy.

Title: Strength and Peace for His People
Promise: The LORD will give strength to his people and bless his people with peace. Doubt: Combines two substances already covered separately: 'Strength for the Weak' (Isaiah 40) and 'Peace in Trouble' (John 14).

Title: Everlasting Mercy to Covenant-Keepers
Promise: The LORD's mercy rests from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness extends to their children's children, to those who keep his covenant and remember his commandments. Doubt: Overlaps 'Never Left nor Forsaken'; Psalms 103:3 is already cited inside the existing healing entry, so this is the closest genuinely distinct Psalms 103 substance, but it may still be too close to existing faithfulness promises. Possible secondary covenant: Mosaic.
Condition: Fearing the LORD, keeping his covenant, and remembering his commandments.

Title: An Everlasting Priest After Melchizedek
Promise: By an unchangeable oath, the LORD appointed the one addressed to a permanent priesthood patterned on Melchizedek's. Doubt: A genuine divine oath, but addressed to the Messiah rather than a promise made to believers generally; prophetic in character. Secondary covenant: New Covenant.

Title: The Son's Inheritance
Promise: The LORD declared the one addressed to be his Son and committed to give him the nations as his inheritance and the ends of the earth as his possession. Doubt: A messianic decree to the Son, not a promise to believers; same category doubt as Psalms 110:4. Secondary covenant: New Covenant.
Condition: Asking of the LORD.

Title: The Holy One Not Left in Hell
Promise: God would not abandon the Holy One's soul to the grave nor let him see corruption, but would show him the path of life with fulness of joy in his presence. Doubt: Messianic prophecy combined with personal confidence; not a stated commitment to believers generally. Secondary covenant: New Covenant.

Title: The King Delivers the Needy
Promise: The king will rescue the needy who cry out, the poor, and those with no helper, sparing the poor and needy and saving their souls. Doubt: Describes the (messianic) king's reign rather than a direct divine promise in God's voice; overlaps the clear Psalms 41 entry on care for the poor.

Title: The LORD Will Perfect What Concerns Me
Promise: The LORD will bring to completion everything that concerns the speaker, since his mercy endures for ever. Doubt: A personal confidence statement rather than a general divine commitment; scope is one speaker's affairs.

Title: Near to Those Who Call, Fulfilling Their Desire
Promise: The LORD is near to all who call on him in truth, fulfils the desire of those who fear him, hears their cry, saves them, and preserves all who love him. Doubt: Overlaps 'Prayer According to His Will' (call/answer) and 'Refuge and Protection' (preservation).
Condition: Calling on him in truth; fearing him; loving him.

Title: Blessing on Those Who Fear the LORD
Promise: The LORD, who has been mindful of his people, will bless them: he will bless those who fear him, small and great alike. Doubt: 'He will bless' states no specific promised action; generic blessing overlaps the Abrahamic blessing entry's theme.
Condition: Fearing the LORD.

Title: Reaping in Joy After Sowing in Tears
Promise: Those who sow in tears will reap in joy, and the one who goes out weeping with seed will return rejoicing with sheaves. Doubt: An agricultural proverb-pattern, not a divine commitment; no divine speaker or promise verb.

Title: Redemption of Israel from All Iniquities
Promise: Mercy and abundant power to redeem belong to the LORD, and he will rescue Israel from every one of its sins. Doubt: National redemption wording; overlaps the existing 'Forgiveness on Confession' entry's pardon substance.
Condition: Hoping in the LORD.

Title: The LORD's Care for the Oppressed and Needy
Promise: The LORD executes judgment for the oppressed, feeds the hungry, frees prisoners, opens blind eyes, lifts the bowed down, loves the righteous, preserves strangers, and relieves the fatherless and widow. Doubt: Present-tense descriptions of God's character and habitual action, not future commitments; partly overlaps the clear Psalms 12:5 entry.

Title: Favour as a Shield Around the Righteous
Promise: The LORD will bless the righteous and surround them with favour as with a shield. Doubt: Single-verse favour statement; blessing/protection substance overlaps 'Refuge and Protection'.

Title: The Cause of the Afflicted Maintained
Promise: The LORD takes up the legal case of the suffering and defends what the poor are owed. Doubt: Stated as the psalmist's confidence ('I know that...') and overlaps the clear Psalms 12:5 entry.

Title: Life For Evermore Where Unity Dwells
Promise: Where brothers dwell together in unity, the LORD has ordained blessing in the form of unending life. Doubt: 'Commanded blessing' is indirect; 'life for evermore' overlaps the existing 'Eternal Life to Believers' entry.
Condition: Dwelling together in unity.

Title: Blessing on the One Who Fears the LORD
Promise: Everyone who fears the LORD and walks in his ways is blessed, eating the labour of their hands, happy and well. Doubt: Wisdom-pattern blessedness (prosperity follows godliness) rather than a divine commitment.
Condition: Fearing the LORD and walking in his ways.

Title: Wisdom Pours Out Her Spirit
Promise: Wisdom calls those addressed to turn at her reproof, committing to pour out her spirit on them and make her words known to them. Doubt: The speaker is personified Wisdom, not God or a prophet speaking in God's voice, so it falls strictly outside the definition; included only because the first-person commitment wording is promise-like.
Condition: Turning at reproof.

Title: The Suffering Servant
Promise: A servant would bear the griefs and sorrows of others, suffer in their place for their wrongdoing, and through that suffering bring them wholeness and peace. Doubt: Prophetic portrait of atonement, not phrased as a divine commitment to a recipient; its force as a promise rests on later application to Christ rather than on a stated 'I will' commitment in the passage itself.
Fulfillment: The Gospels and epistles apply the servant's suffering to Jesus.

Title: David and the Levites Never Lack a Man
Promise: David would never lack a man to sit on Israel's throne, nor would the Levitical priests lack a man to offer sacrifices, secured by the same fixed covenant as day and night. Doubt: The Davidic half is a genuine promise, but the Levitical offering perpetuity sits in tension with Hebrews' teaching that sacrifices have ceased; drafting both halves as one fulfilled promise would overstate the case.

Title: Seventy Weeks to Finish Transgression
Promise: Seventy weeks were determined for Daniel's people and city to finish transgression, end sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up vision and prophecy, and anoint the most Holy. Doubt: A prophetic timetable and revelation, not a simple divine commitment; its dating and the identity of its fulfilment events are heavily debated, so it does not cleanly fit the definition.

Title: Revived on the Third Day
Promise: After two days his people would be revived, and on the third day raised up, so they would live in his sight, as surely as the morning and the latter rain come. Doubt: The words are the people's resolve and hopeful expectation ('let us return'), not God speaking a promise; the third-day language is also debated and should not be forced into a resurrection promise.
Condition: Returning to the LORD, as Hosea 6:1 urges.

Title: The LORD Will Not Cast Off Forever
Promise: The LORD would not cast off forever, but though he causes grief he would have compassion according to his many mercies, since he does not willingly afflict or grieve the children of men. Doubt: A general theological assurance in a lament, not a specific divine commitment to a named recipient; Lamentations contains no oracle addressed as a promise, so this is the closest candidate and remains doubtful.

Title: Good Tidings of Peace for Judah
Promise: Good tidings of peace would be brought to Judah, her feasts kept and vows performed, for the wicked would no longer pass through her, being utterly cut off. Doubt: Judah's deliverance here is an implied consequence of Nineveh's fall, not a standalone commitment addressed to Judah; the feast-keeping is a command rather than a promise condition, so the entry would rest on implication.

Title: Living by Faith
Promise: The righteous person would live by trusting God, in contrast to the proud soul that is not upright. Doubt: A principle or maxim about how the just live, not a divine commitment to do something; its importance in the New Testament does not turn it into a promise in Habakkuk's own form.
Condition: Faith, as opposed to pride.
Fulfillment: Paul and Hebrews quote this line for life by faith.

Title: The Earth Filled With Knowledge of the LORD's Glory
Promise: The earth would be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea. Doubt: A universal prophetic vision with no named recipient and no 'I will' commitment form; it is closer to an eschatological vision than to a promise of God in the collection's defined sense.

Title: Kingdom Blessings in the Beatitudes
Promise: In the kingdom of heaven, the poor in spirit, those who mourn, the meek, those hungering for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, and those persecuted for righteousness receive comfort, mercy, the earth as inheritance, satisfaction, sonship, sight of God, and great reward.
KeyScriptures: Matthew 5:3; Matthew 5:4; Matthew 5:5; Matthew 5:6; Matthew 5:7; Matthew 5:8; Matthew 5:9; Matthew 5:10; Matthew 5:11; Matthew 5:12

Title: The Spirit Will Speak for Persecuted Disciples
Promise: When disciples are handed over for Christ's sake, they need not rehearse a defence in advance, because the Spirit of the Father will supply the words in that very hour.
Condition: Being handed over to councils and rulers for Christ's sake

Title: Confessed Before the Father
Promise: Whoever openly acknowledges Christ before people will be acknowledged by Christ before the Father in heaven.
Condition: Openly acknowledging Christ before people

Title: Christ Will Build His Church
Promise: Christ will build his church, and the powers of death will not overcome it; to his people he gives the keys of the kingdom, with authority to bind and loose, and sins remitted or retained accordingly.

Title: Thrones for the Apostles
Promise: In the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, the apostles will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, eating and drinking at his table in his kingdom.

Title: A Hundredfold for Forsaking All
Promise: Whoever leaves houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or lands for Christ's name will receive many times as much in this life and will inherit eternal life.
Condition: Leaving houses, family, or lands for Christ's name

Title: Endurance to the End
Promise: The one who endures to the end will be saved.
Condition: Enduring to the end

Title: The Kingdom Prepared from the Foundation
Promise: At the judgment, the righteous will be invited to inherit the kingdom prepared for them from the foundation of the world.

Title: Many from East and West at the Patriarchs' Table
Promise: Many will come from east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

Title: Christ With His People Always
Promise: The risen Christ is with his people always, even to the end of the age, as they go and teach all nations.

Title: Drinking New in the Father's Kingdom
Promise: Christ will drink the fruit of the vine new with his people in his Father's kingdom.

Title: The Kingdom Given by the Father's Pleasure
Promise: It is the Father's good pleasure to give the kingdom to his little flock, so they need not fear.

Title: Authority Over the Enemy
Promise: Christ gives his followers authority over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will by any means harm them.

Title: Power from on High
Promise: The promise of the Father would come upon the apostles, clothing them with power from on high to be witnesses to the ends of the earth.
Condition: Waiting in Jerusalem as commanded
Fulfillment: Acts 2:1-4 records the Spirit coming upon the apostles at Pentecost with power.

Title: Children of God to All Who Receive Him
Promise: To everyone who receives Christ and believes in his name, God gives the right to become a child of God, born not of blood or human will but of God.
Condition: Receiving Christ and believing in his name

Title: Living Water That Never Runs Dry
Promise: Whoever drinks the water Christ gives will never thirst again, because it becomes a spring of water welling up to eternal life within them.

Title: Never Cast Out
Promise: All who come to Christ will never hunger or thirst, and Christ will never cast out anyone who comes to him.
Condition: Coming to Christ

Title: The Light of Life
Promise: Whoever follows Christ will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life.
Condition: Following Christ

Title: Freedom Through the Truth
Promise: Those who continue in Christ's word are truly his disciples, and they will know the truth, and the truth will set them free.
Condition: Continuing in Christ's word

Title: All Drawn to the Lifted-Up Christ
Promise: When Christ is lifted up from the earth, he will draw all people to himself.

Title: The Father Honours Christ's Servants
Promise: Where Christ is, his servant will be also, and the Father will honour whoever serves Christ.
Condition: Serving and following Christ

Title: One Fold and One Shepherd
Promise: Christ's other sheep will hear his voice, and there will be one flock under one shepherd.

Title: Christ Manifest and Indwelling
Promise: Christ manifests himself to those who love him and keep his word, and he and the Father make their home with them, and they abide in his love.
Condition: Loving Christ and keeping his word

Title: Guided Into All Truth
Promise: The Spirit of truth will guide believers into all truth, speaking what he hears and declaring things to come.

Title: Sorrow Turned to Joy
Promise: Believers' sorrow will be turned into joy, a joy no one can take away, and they will rejoice with exceeding joy when Christ's glory is revealed.

Title: Happy in Doing What Is Known
Promise: Those who know Christ's teaching and do it are blessed.
Condition: Knowing and doing Christ's teaching

Title: With Christ Where He Is
Promise: Believers will be with Christ where he is and behold his glory, the glory given him by the Father.

Title: Times of Refreshing
Promise: When people repent and turn, times of refreshing will come from the presence of the Lord, and God will send Jesus Christ, whom heaven must receive until the restoration of all things.
Condition: Repentance and conversion

Title: Glory to Be Revealed
Promise: The sufferings of this present time cannot compare with the glory that will be revealed in believers, who are predestined to be conformed to Christ and glorified, shining like the sun in the Father's kingdom.

Title: All Things for Good
Promise: For those who love God and are called according to his purpose, all things work together for good.
Condition: Loving God and being called according to his purpose

Title: All Israel Shall Be Saved
Promise: When the Deliverer comes from Zion, all Israel will be saved, as God turns ungodliness away from Jacob under his covenant to take away their sins.

Title: Reigning in Life by Grace
